BAGONG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City SEP 16 2025 www.dilg.gov.ph OPINION NO. S. 2025 MS. NHORYAH P. LALONG Former Sangguniang Barangay Member Brgy. Bongbong, Pantukan Davao de Oro Dear Ms. Lalong: This pertains to your earlier letter concerning the propriety of your reappointment as former Sangguniang Barangay (SB) member of Barangay Bongbong, Pantukan, Davao de Oro, to your previous post as SB member in the said Barangay. As represented, on June 20, 2024, you resigned from your position as an SB member due to personal matters and pressure from the Punong Barangay regarding your absences. It is intimated that you have now resolved your personal concerns, and your constituents have expressed their desire for you to return to your post. Ostensibly, the position is still vacant, as no person has yet been appointed to fill up the said position. Hence, the subject query. In response thereto, this Department is of the opinion that your reappointment to your previous post, after your resignation therefrom, would be improper. It is to be noted that resignation is a mode of terminating official relations to one's office. It implies an expression of the incumbent in some form, express or implied, of the intention to surrender, renounce, and relinquish the office and its acceptance by competent and lawful authority. 1 Along this line, this Department is cognizant of the constitutional dictum that a "public office is a public trust." When one seeks an elective position and has in fact been elected thereto by the mandate of the electorate who voted him into office, he should assume all the duties and responsibilities pertaining thereto, including the duty to assume a higher office, and he cannot just 'throw off' such responsibilities at his own pleasure, except by tendering his resignation therefrom? Our view finds strong support in jurisprudence. In particular, the Supreme Court, in Civil Service Commission vs. Province of Misamis Orientaß articulated that "quitters are responsible for their own quitting. Persons who willingly turn their backs on their own relations cannot demand to be taken back and restored to their previous state as though nothing happened." DILG Legal Opinion No. 124-93 citing Gamboa v. Court of Appeals, 108 SCRA I; Ortiz v. COMELEC, 162 SCRA 812 2 DILG Legal Opinion No. 063-A-99 3 G.R. No. 211077, August 15, 2018 ' 'Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

Notwithstanding, please note that this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: A Y. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA/RPBfLLLS-LRALLD/jam cc: ABDULLAH V.
